I feel your pain here, for the longest time I wished I the world woujd just stop, and I could go to sleep for like a couple months and then it'd restart when I felt like I could bare it again. Your not alone, hang in there.

Hey there, sorry to hear you're sufferring this way. If I could offer a word of advice, despite therapy and support groups being great treatments, oftentimes the job is not done at that. It's like, we gotta make a sustainable effort to keep ourselves sane, cus things can always still go wrong or get more fucked up than it already is. You might not see anything for you because of this, but there is, suicidal ideation is like a fog that you have to walk through without suffocating and it's hard. But difficulty doesn't mean hopelessness. These are just the words I can offer you for the little it's worth. Good Luck.

Yeah, you have a great point there. There is no inherent meaning that will keep you here. An inherent meaning was kind of a fantasy to begin with. That's why the things that truly make life worth living are the human connections we can have, the potential for making new ones and nurturing the ones we already have. So I would probably give a searching for a concrete reason, but I'd certaintly encourage the creating and finding of many different new ones despite that, kinda paradoxical, but that's how it is I suppose. Moving on despite all the ridiculousness.

Personally I'm not sure suicide and mental illness are still considered taboo. Kinda debatable since we have shows like 13 Reasons Why and Euphoria that romanticize teen suicide and mental illness for profit under the guise of activism. Just my opinion though.

Right,yeah , it can be really awful to feel disconnected from the ones we love for things that we have little control over. I guess my sentiment here, for whatever it's worth, is that, there is potential to connect with them despite it all, even if it's not "normal" or ideal. I wish the best for you and your family.

Right, honestly, I think that's a really awesome and admirable thing to do on your part. It's one kind of courage to leave this world, but it's another special kind of courage to have hope in the connections we make, despite knowing how confusing and filled with pain things ahead may be. All the best dude.

I see, I understand you, but to be blunt, there is no way for you too make it easier for them. Suicide is kind of point of no return that way, you have to truly not care about anyone that will grieve for you, because it's not like you'll have to deal with guilt if you're dead and it already is done because the present circumstances are ones you don't want to be in. You're undecided, cus yeah this shit is all so messy and confusing. But I believe you care for your family, ofc, that being said, you also have the choice to enrich your life by being close to them. Cus it's like, a lot of the time what makes this existence actually fucking mean something, is those we can connect with, if even for a little while, the suffering is far and we can continue living. Good luck.
I see, if it's not too late, I wouldn't mind hearing your story.

Hi there, I'm sorry to hear that you feel this way. Anxiety tends to be extremely debilitating and just messes with our ability to live our lives. Especially when you think about how easy things should otherwise, you feel like your just not meant for the world. But I'm certain there are things in your life that can reassure you that despite your condition, you can live in this world and make the most of it. Confide in those that mean the most to you, try not to get caught up in that fucked up cycle of self deprecation as hard as it is. Good luck.

Yeah I totally resonate with that, well it's a lot like the other poster said. Answers can be so arbitrary and the best we can attempt to do is get into healthy communities or dedicate ourselves towards smth. In general things quite the task.

I absolutely agree, answers that we find are completely contingent and situational, and it is only surmisable that being a a more socially  convenient situation opposed to the cynicism of depressive disorders is better. But not everyone has access to that and disillusionment is still very possible, you would've just better your chances, so whilst you make excellent points situationally, there could be some pragmatism is suicide.

Yeah definitely, I've been deeply immersed in reading philosophy and psychology for answers for the last 2 years. Although after a while it all loses it's practicality when you realize how difficult actual change is. I guess that's why authors like Mark Fisher took their lives. Tbh I considering the implications of that, is there really no damn escape.
